items.label: onsemi Q2 FY2026 (08-03-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CALL — TAMS REWRITTEN AROUND THE GIGAWATT BUILD-OUT

set.signal: CALL — TAMS REWRITTEN AROUND THE GIGAWATT BUILD-OUT: CEO Hassane El-Khoury said the raised AI data center TAM is anchored on 2030 and correlated to 'a gigawatt scale that would be installed by 2030' — the projected installed base converted to the power needed at a data center or rack site, multiplied by onsemi's content per rack — plus a TAM increase across the board from products introduced since the last update (vertical GaN, Treo, SiC JFETs in data centers and in industrial solid-state circuit breakers / solid-state power disconnects). Content math (CEO): on today's $15,000 of content per rack the split is 70% medium-to-low voltage and 30% high voltage; at $115,000 of content it becomes 50/50 — 'One is going up 10, one is going up 5x to 6x', the outsize increase in high voltage. 800 V timing: an 800 V DC rack is a step function in content, but revenue ramps gradually with the build-out, starting 'end of 2027, beginning of 2028, give or take a quarter'; 'we're already starting to see some platform' designs with vertical GaN and JFET content. Growth vectors: SiC revenue in AI data center applications expected to grow nearly 60% year over year in 2026; SiC revenue in China EVs expected to increase between 60% and 70% on share gains (China automotive revenue up 13% in H1 2026 against total vehicle sales down 4%; Rivian R2 zonal MOSFETs and SiC onboard charging in the US); ESS revenue expected to grow approximately 40% in 2026 (AI halo, North America microgrid customers; next-generation EliteSiC hybrid ESS module at 99.3% efficiency; sampling a 500 kW hybrid module platform with 20% higher power density). EV TAM drivers (CEO): EVs as a higher percent of SAR, higher SiC penetration within EVs, hybrid design wins in China and North America, Treo (10BASE-T1S, ultrasonic sensing) and onboard charging — 'a bottoms-up TAM adjustment' done for Analyst Day. AI data center revenue is 'very equal' across the power tree ('from the wall to the core'); AI data center is primarily US, with some China starting via Great Wall. Q3 mix (CFO Thad Trent): auto up low single digits, industrial relatively flat, other (including AI data center) up high teens.
set.figure: Content per rack $15,000 (70% mid/low voltage, 30% high voltage) -> $115,000 (50/50; high voltage up 10x, mid/low 5x-6x); 800V ramp end-2027 / early-2028; SiC in AI DC nearly +60% in 2026

items.reason: The TAM figures (~$12B -> ~$48-50B AI data center; $26B -> $63B EV) were stated only by analysts (Susquehanna, Mizuho) in their questions; the CEO explained the drivers but did not state or confirm the numbers, and the release does not carry them. Also 'nearly 60%' (not ~60%) for SiC in AI data center; attribution restored.
items.evidence: In 2026, we expect our silicon carbide revenue in AI data center applications to grow nearly 60% year-over-year.

items.label: onsemi Q2 FY2026 (08-03-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CALL — SUPPLY IS TIGHTENING AND AI-DC GETS PRIORITY

set.signal: CALL — SUPPLY IS TIGHTENING AND AI-DC GETS PRIORITY: CEO Hassane El-Khoury: 'Supply is tightening in several growth areas, lead times are extending, and we are seeing increases in both orders placed within lead time and customer escalations'. CFO Thad Trent: lead time 'stretched out from about 27 weeks to somewhere around 32 weeks on average' across the portfolio; book-to-bill 'significantly above one for several quarters and continued to strengthen'; 'We're getting better visibility even into 2027', with 'some customers ordering out into 2028 trying to lock up supply'. In Q2 onsemi prioritized shipments to AI data center over automotive and industrial (CFO: expected to normalize as supply rebalances to match demand; CEO: manufacturing output catching up in the third and fourth quarter; CFO: a fab cycle time of four to six months). Utilization rose to 83% from 77% (CEO: 92%-93% is fully utilized, then onsemi flexes to the outside, and revenue is 'still 25%, 30% higher than the run-rate today' before it gets capped; CFO: about a two-quarter lag to the P&L and 25-30 basis points of gross margin per point of utilization). Pricing: input costs rising (CFO: raw materials and external manufacturing; CEO: substrates or gold) -> a second round of price increases with the benefit over the next several quarters, plus 'surgical' increases where there is allocation; CEO: 'nothing is coming down, and therefore, I'm not expecting a softer pricing environment in 2027 either.' Non-core exits done: the final $35 million in Q2 (roughly $300 million for the year; about $900 million exited over the last few years); announced divestitures of the Mountain Top and Philippines manufacturing facilities (approximately $35 million of annualized savings, initial benefit in 2027 and full savings in 2028; approximately 50 of the 200 basis points of planned FabRight gross margin improvement). CEO: 'from our perspective, we're not seeing an inventory build' — shipping to end demand; distribution inventory 10.1 weeks (from 10.8) with sell-through outpacing sell-in; mass market revenue up 20% sequentially.

items.reason: Restores attribution (CEO vs CFO) and the CEO's hedge on customer inventory ('from our perspective'); the Mountain Top and Philippines fabs are announced divestitures, not completed ones.
items.evidence: The announced divestitures of our Mountain Top and Philippines manufacturing facilities further advances our FabRight strategy
